reply_text:
㊥ (why the page looks stalled) You're right that the page stopped showing progress, and the reason is mine: nothing has been merged into the integration branch since 18:12, more than three hours ago. The loss and correctness charts only measure merged, Lean-checked rows. The update loop is still running, but every new snapshot came out the same, so no new points appeared. Tonight's work is on ten unmerged branches, and the page showed none of it.

㊢ (what I changed on the page) I added an "In flight" table, which you can see now. It lists every unmerged branch:
- what it fixes, with the Lean reference;
- how many rows wait on it;
- what stage it's at;
- the time of the last merge into cand-1.

The "rows blocked by each stop" chart did get new points at 20:37, 20:52 and 21:07, from the rows we re-probed, but it doesn't show branch work either.

🈖 (why nothing merged) I've held every fix to two checks: a test that fails before the fix on the actual defect, and cold acceptance. Most of tonight went into getting the first right. Four tests failed for the wrong reason, two fixes guessed at Lean's behaviour, and A and B turned out to depend on each other. Each cold acceptance takes 25 to 60 minutes. Several fixes are near the end now:

| branch | waiting on it | stage |
|---|---|---|
| `psw/nullrecv` | 11 rows | cold acceptance running, likely done around 22:50 |
| `psw/termquot` (A) | ~45 rows, with B | cold acceptance running |
| `psw/estout` | 3 rows | cold acceptance running |
| `psw/hostparsers` | 3 rows | cold acceptance running |

🈳 (what to expect) Merging moves rows to their next stop, not necessarily to correct. So the loss may move little even after these merges, but the blocked-rows chart should drop when `psw/nullrecv` lands. I'll merge each branch as soon as its acceptance passes rather than batching, and update the in-flight table as stages change.

previous_reply_acts.text: (the movement chart) It's at https://zone.hyperreal.enterprises/wip/mfuton-progress.html, and I checked a rendered screenshot. It shows the pattern I described earlier. "Source projection" climbed to 43 rows during the afternoon, then fell to 4 when the `term[_]` merge landed. In the same step, "`term[_]` quotation coercion" jumped from 2 to 38. Right now the stops are:

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text:
(finding the next stops)
- **codex-6** is re-probing the 45 rows that haven't been probed since the `term[_]` merge. It runs 4 lanes, warm, which is fine for discovery, and groups the rows by their current stop.
- **codex-25** is finding what the `term[_]`-blocked rows hit after that stop, before the real fix lands. It uses codex-18's rejected shortcut, which gives the type Lean uses for these rows' case, applied only in its own worktrees. Those results are recorded under a commit name that isn't on cand-1, so they can't count towards the curve.
- **claude-3** is tracing the `null.<field>` stop (5 rows that never reach `term[_]`) in Lean. That becomes a packet for another idle seat.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (Rob's main) Understood. The dropped work is restored: codex-4 classified every change of Rob's that the merge dropped. The 6 that mattered are back in `d6b0b096`, including the three definitions his code calls, which had stopped the merge from loading. The other 12 are recorded with the cand-1 commit that covers each one, or the reason for our choice. The five-row cold check is the last gate. If it passes, I'll check the merge in to Rob's main and report the commit.
